dedupe_keys.name: zema german central reporting and evaluation office for major accidents and incidents in process plants uba online database

description: Germany's national database of reportable accidents and incidents at plants covered by the Major Accidents Ordinance (12. BImSchV, the German Seveso implementation). The UBA pages say ZEMA was set up in the German Environment Agency in 1993 to record and evaluate all reportable events, which are divided by hazard potential into major accidents (Störfälle) and disruptions of normal operation, publishes annual reports, and holds more than 570 detailed national reports that can be searched in its online database with filters for date, location, plant type and more; since 1999 its web portal has also offered German, European and international information on accidents with hazardous substances. The database is free to search online; bulk download and licence are not stated on the pages read. Coverage is Germany from 1993. Caveats: reportable events only, in German, and searchable, not downloadable. For simulation it gives German accident histories by plant type and cause, to set event rates and consequences in chemical plant risk models. Related catalogue records include eMARS and the French ARIA database.
